ch1.title: The pause no one designed for
ch1.caption: One car charging at the edge of an otherwise empty forecourt. The infrastructure provides power, but little reason to stay.

1-1.title: A new road system
1-1.caption: Transmission lines and roads cross the same landscape. Pylons stand on open ground beyond the highway, with their conductors visible against white. Interpretive architectural landscape study.

1-2.title: The railway built a civic room
1-2.caption: An enclosed hall gives people room to sit, meet and wait, with shops and cafés at its edges. Interpretive study inspired by Pennsylvania Station.

1-2.title: The road built a canopy
1-2.caption: A canopy shelters fuel islands and a pay booth: a brief vehicle transaction, with no public waiting room.

1-2.title: Charging inherited the forecourt
1-2.caption: The stop gets longer, but the layout stays a forecourt. People wait inside cars, lean beside them or sit on the kerb.

1-3.title: Twenty minutes
1-3.caption: A coffee beside the car at a highway charging stop.

1-3.title: One to two hours
1-3.caption: A delivery driver eating lunch on the van step, with nowhere to sit.

1-3.title: A night
1-3.caption: Electric trucks parked after an overnight legal rest; a driver crosses the lot to the showers.

1-4.title: A charger is not a place
1-4.caption: A mostly empty parking lot with charging bays along one edge, but no public programme.

1-4.title: Programme makes the place
1-4.caption: The same ground gains a two-storey public building: market and clinic below, shared workspace and community rooms above.

1-5.title: Freight corridor
1-5.caption: Truck charging bays at early morning, with rooms, showers and a kitchen for drivers behind them.

1-5.title: City
1-5.caption: Chargers at ground level, a gym and workspace above, a public corner plaza.

1-5.title: Town
1-5.caption: A market hall and clinic around a courtyard, with a few cars charging along one side.

1-6.title: The proposition
1-6.caption: An unresolved circular field suggests charging, public life and open ground; the architectural form remains to be designed.

1-7.title: Sustainability: its ground and energy
1-7.caption: A solar roof over the bays, with battery storage behind a screen.

1-7.title: Phenomenology: the pause itself
1-7.caption: A quiet room looking out on the bays, someone reading in the low sun.

1-7.title: Social theory: who the place is for
1-7.caption: Shared tables in an open courtyard, visible from the street.

ch2.title: The ground built for standing
ch2.caption: A suburban edge from above: far more tarmac than building.

2-1.title: The ground as found
2-1.caption: Cracked, unshaded asphalt in summer heat.

2-1.title: The ground re-made
2-1.caption: The same view with shade, planting, permeable paving and a protected path.

2-2.title: Charging where life happens
2-2.caption: A car completing an overnight charge in a home garage, early morning.

2-2.title: Nowhere to charge at home
2-2.caption: An apartment street in early morning, cars parked kerb to kerb and no chargers.

2-3.title: Caravanserai
2-3.caption: One gate and a shared court: courtyard of the Mahyar caravanserai, Iran. Eugène Flandin, 1840; public domain.

2-3.title: Coaching inn
2-3.caption: Galleries over the coach yard: the George Inn, Southwark, 1889. Public domain.

2-3.title: Railway terminal
2-3.caption: A public concourse: main concourse, Grand Central Terminal, New York, c. 1913. Detroit Publishing Co., Library of Congress; public domain.

2-3.title: Airport terminal
2-3.caption: Waiting as experience: TWA Flight Center, New York (Saarinen, 1962). Photograph 2019, Wikimedia Commons; CC0.

2-4.title: Every vehicle, a different pause
2-4.caption: E-bike, motorcycle, car, van, bus and truck plugged in side by side.

2-5.title: The rules of the stop
2-5.caption: A driver resting in the cab in early morning, the truck charging outside.

2-6.title: The literal powerhouse
2-6.caption: Solar roof, battery room, charging bays and public rooms in one architectural study.

2-6.title: Lights on when the grid fails
2-6.caption: The neighbourhood dark in a power cut; the Powerhouse lit and full of people.

ch3.title: A new kind of station
ch3.caption: A public hall with a food hall, market and benches, where the charging bays are seen through one glazed edge and most people have no vehicle to charge.

3-1.title: Nothing to sit on
3-1.caption: A charging lot beside the highway: one person on the kerb, no bench, no shade, no toilet.

3-1.title: Five needs, provided
3-1.caption: A shaded plaza beside the bays: seats, water, toilets, food, play and something to watch.

3-2.title: Michi-no-eki
3-2.caption: A Japanese roadside station: parking and rest for travellers, a market and a hall for the town.

3-2.title: Market day, no plug
3-2.caption: The bays stand empty while the plaza, market, clinic and playground are full.

3-3.title: A row of posts
3-3.caption: The visible face of the transition: charging posts in the corner of a car park.

3-3.title: An icon with a public programme
3-3.caption: A building whose structure, roof and light make the energy visible, with open ground in front.

3-4.title: Dark lot
3-4.caption: Asphalt at noon, a driver waiting in the car, nowhere else to wait.

3-4.title: Green ground
3-4.caption: The same bays between trees and canopies, on ground that takes the rain.

3-5.title: Eleven at night
3-5.caption: The open ground lit and in use; the hall and market shut; the operated rooms keeping their own hours.

3-6.title: A type, not a building
3-6.caption: The same charger with different rooms around it: along a highway, on a city block, beside a town.

ch4.title: Node and place
ch4.caption: A Powerhouse between the road network on one side and a neighbourhood on the other.

4-1.title: Reading a site
4-1.caption: A road, a rail line, a substation, an old garage and a neighbourhood meeting at one corner, and no charger yet. Any site; the reading comes first.

4-2.title: Freight corridor
4-2.caption: Spread along the road: truck bays at the front, rooms for a night set back.

4-2.title: City
4-2.caption: Compact and stacked: charging below, public rooms above, a roof garden.

4-2.title: Town
4-2.caption: A civic hall with a market, clinic and hall, and charging alongside.

4-3.title: The rules, lifted apart
4-3.caption: Ground, bays, rooms and roof as the layers of one building.

4-4.title: Seven in the morning
4-4.caption: Commuters, fleet drivers and the market being set up.

4-4.title: Two in the morning
4-4.caption: Drivers on their rest, a night-shift worker, a lit and open waiting room.

4-5.title: A timed count
4-5.caption: Who is where, doing what, from above: people gather where there is shade and a seat.

4-6.title: One Powerhouse
4-6.caption: The principles in one building: a public court, an energy roof, green ground, an icon that is theirs to use.
